info.bio:
Se puede decir que son la banda australiana más famosa de todos los tiempos después de AC/DC. Más populares aún que INXS o la Little River Band, Men At Work es la única agrupación de esas tierras que ha logrado ocupar el primer lugar tanto en Estados Unidos con sencillos y con álbumes.

La historia de Men At Work empieza con el cantante Colin Hay, nacido y criado en Escocia. Su padre tenía una tienda de artículos musicales en Glasgow. Fue allí donde aprendió a tocar todos los instrumentos.

scenes.name: Pop de Australia y Nueva Zelanda
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Australia aporta las elegías neorrománticas de los Go-Betweens, las microsinfonías de The Church, Hunters And Collectors, Midnight Oil, Men At Work, Triffids e INXS. Nueva Zelanda cría una generación de antihéroes que no tiene nada que ver con la ola británica comercial y crea el género de los noventa: el «lo-fi pop». The Clean (como si los Buzzcocks versionaran a Syd Barrett y a la Velvet), Tall Dwarfs, Chills, Bats, This Kind Of Punishment, Jean Paul Sartre Experience, Scorched Earth Policy, Able Tasmans, Verlaines y la figura de Peter Jefferies.

podcast.title: Australian Band with Brit-Style New Wave
podcast.body: This Australian band achieved significant success in the US with a sound that blended Brit-style new wave, heavy saxophone, and tropical rhythms. "Around the same time an Australian band called Men at Work did even better. Their debut album, Business as usual, a blend of Brit style new wave, heavy saxophone and tropical rhythms, spent a staggering 15 weeks at number one in the U.S."

podcast.title: Not an Imperial Act
podcast.body: Despite their initial massive success, including back-to-back number one hits and an album that topped the charts for 15 weeks, Men at Work were not considered an imperial act. Their hits quickly dried up, they never achieved a fifth top 10 hit, and their sound neither influenced other acts nor consistently connected on the airwaves, indicating they were "a momentarily big act that were never imperial." "Men at work were a momentarily big act that were never imperial."
